name: Geo Stamp
tagline: Stamp the device's location, and optionally a photo, onto a record.
summary:
Records where somebody was standing when they filled in a record, into a text column you already have, with one button. On a phone, the same press can attach a photo.

- Says plainly when location is not available, which is the case for a model-driven form open in a browser
- Records an imprecise reading and says how far off it might be, rather than refusing it

Location works in canvas apps and in the model-driven mobile app.

limitations: The location is simulated. On the Power Apps mobile app, Record location reads the device's position; the demo cannot reach yours, so the Stamping on the mobile app preset answers context.device.getCurrentPosition() with a fixed reading — 47.620422, -122.349358, accurate to 8 m — and the event log under the demo says so. What the control does with it is real: the readout, the precision, the accuracy label and the latitude and longitude outputs. The other presets declare no position, so Record location reports that the reading could not be taken, which is the honest answer on a model-driven form in a desktop browser: getCurrentPosition is documented for canvas apps and the mobile client only.

Add photo works against the demo's stand-in Dataverse. The demo's form is an account, Northwind Traders, with a Notes table behind it, so the control finds the model-driven route it needs. On the Stamping on the mobile app preset, captureImage opens your browser's own file picker in place of the camera — the picture is real, the camera is not — and the control resolves the table through utils.getEntityMetadata and writes a Note with webAPI.createRecord, bound to the account; the lastNoteId output shows the new Note. Nothing leaves the browser. On the other presets captureImage is refused, as on a desktop form, and the control says the photo could not be saved.

The map is off, and turning it on is a licensing decision rather than a display one. It loads a tile from tile.openstreetmap.org, which is why the manifest declares external-service-usage and why any app containing this component is a premium app. Everything else the control does works with it off.

A recorded location, Fewer decimal places and Nothing recorded yet hand the control a coordinate directly, or none, the way a saved record would. That is the state after a stamp, or before one — the readout, the precision, the accuracy label and the theming are all real.

presets.name: Stamping on the mobile app
presets.description: An empty record on the Power Apps mobile app. Record location takes a simulated reading, and Add photo saves a picture you choose as a note on the record — as the camera and GPS would.

presets.name: A recorded location
presets.description: A column that already holds a reading, which is what most people see most of the time — the control spends far more of its life displaying a stamp than taking one.

presets.name: Fewer decimal places
presets.description: The same reading at two decimal places — about a kilometre. Six is the default because it is finer than any consumer GPS resolves; fewer is a deliberate choice to record roughly where somebody was rather than exactly.

presets.name: Nothing recorded yet
presets.description: The empty state, which says so rather than showing a blank box. This is what a new record looks like before anyone presses anything.
